reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The test still uses hand-written checks instead of the testify assertions required by the repository’s test guidelines.
1 open issue - [Use testify assertions instead of manual test checks](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/pull/27984#discussion_r4503437937) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes #27980 by routing `SettingSelector.AcceptDateTime` to the `Accept-Datetime` header instead of the pagination query parameter in Azure App Configuration list requests. **Changes:** - Corrects the settings and revisions option converters. - Adds regression coverage for all three selector converters. - Documents the fix in the changelog. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `sdk/​data/​azappconfig/​setting_selector.go` | Maps the timestamp to `AcceptDatetime` in both affected converters. | | `sdk/​data/​azappconfig/​setting_selector_test.go` | Checks timestamp mapping and verifies `After` remains unset for list operations. | | `sdk/​data/​azappconfig/​CHANGELOG.md` | Records the header-mapping fix. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: nit: The repository's test guidelines require testify assertions rather than hand-written `if`/`t.Errorf` checks. Replace these checks throughout this test with `assert.Nil` for `After` and `assert.Equal(t, &want, ...AcceptDatetime)`; the latter compares the pointed-to values without risking a nil dereference and reports the timestamp on failure.
